Attached: 1 image

Nineteen directories, and I still had to look half of them up the first time someone asked me what they do.

/proc and /sys are not real files, I learned. The kernel makes them up on the fly to expose what is happening inside it right now. /var is the one that quietly fills your disk while you are not looking, logs and caches, growing without asking. /opt exists purely so vendors have somewhere to put things without touching anything Linux itself owns.

Everything on this list hangs off the same root. One slash, nineteen jobs.
